transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Well, I suppose what brings me in is... this memorial I'm putting together for my brother. It's just gotten a lot bigger than I originally meant it to. 

I’ve been spending most of my days chasing down songs, calling folks up, planning out these displays and even trips for it. It takes up all my time right now. My wife is the one who made a point of it, really—she says I’ve completely pushed aside the garden, my walking group, and just about everything else I usually do. So, that's why I'm here.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy things as much as you usually would, or that activities you normally like doing feel less rewarding lately?

No, I wouldn't say that. It's not that I don't enjoy the garden or walking anymore. I just... well, I don't have the time for them right now. 

The memorial is just taking up all my energy. I still like my usual hobbies just fine, I just haven't been doing them because I'm so focused on getting this project right. It's not a lack of enjoyment, it's just a lack of hours in the day.
Outside of focusing on the memorial, have you noticed any other areas of your life where you feel unusually stuck, distressed, or unable to stop thinking about something?

No, not really. I mean, the memorial is pretty much the only thing on my mind right now. I don't feel stuck or distressed about anything else. It's just this one big project that's got all my attention, you know? I haven't noticed any other thoughts taking over like this.
Have you noticed any difficulties in your relationships, work, or other important areas of life because of how much time and energy you're putting into the memorial?

Well, I suppose it has, yes. Like I said before, I've completely let the garden go. And I've been missing my walking group and my book club. I've actually upset some of my friends down at the senior center, too, because... well, everything with me has just become about this memorial display, and they get tired of hearing about it.

And at home, it's been tough on my wife. She says our whole day just revolves around her having to calm me down or redirect me. She feels like she's always having to stop me from making another phone call, or planning another trip, or getting into an argument with somebody over the details. So, yes, it's definitely putting a strain on things.
Do you feel like you can't resist the urge to keep working on the memorial, even when you know you should be focusing on something else or when it's causing problems?

No, I wouldn't say it's like that. It's not some... urge I'm trying to fight off, or anything. 

I mean, I know it causes some trouble at home like I said, but I don't sit there thinking I shouldn't be working on it. I don't feel like I have to force myself to stop, or that I'm doing something I know I shouldn't be doing. It just feels like important work that needs to get done, so... I do it. I'm not really trying to resist it at all.
Even though you feel that working on the memorial is something you should be doing, do you feel any internal conflict or frustration about how much it's taking over your life?

No, I don't really feel frustrated about it. I mean, I know my wife gets frustrated, and my friends are annoyed, but for me... no. I don't feel any conflict. Like I said, it's just something important that I have to do. It doesn't bother me that it's taking up my time, because it's exactly what I should be doing right now.
Have you ever thought to yourself that your focus on the memorial might be going too far, or that you might be taking it to an extreme that other people wouldn't find necessary?

No, not really. I mean, I know other people think that, like my wife and the folks at the senior center. They probably think it's extreme. But to me? No. I don't think I'm taking it too far at all. It's just a big project, and it needs to be done right. So, no, I haven't ever sat there and thought I was going overboard with it.
Have you noticed any periods of time where you felt unusually energized, where you needed less sleep, or where your thoughts were racing faster than usual while working on the memorial?

Well, I definitely have a lot of energy right now. I just can't seem to sit in my chair like I used to. I'm... I'm up all the time, hauling boxes around, making phone calls, rearranging all my papers for the memorial. I just keep walking from room to room. Honestly, it feels like my body has more steam in it than a man my age ought to have. So, yes, I guess you could say I'm unusually energized.
Have you been sleeping less than usual lately, or do you feel like you don’t need as much sleep while you're working on the memorial?

I don't think so. I mean, I haven't really been watching the clock, but... no, I haven't noticed sleeping any less than I usually do. I still go to bed when my wife does. I guess I just wake up ready to get back to the project, but I wouldn't say I feel like I don't need sleep or anything like that. I'm just getting my regular rest and then getting right back to work.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, overly optimistic, or expansive — like you're feeling on top of the world or unusually confident — while working on the memorial?

Yeah, I suppose you could say that. I mean, I'll feel... well, just lit up, you know? Really full of purpose one minute. I get this strong feeling that the whole town is finally going to understand our family once the memorial is up. 

But then... it kind of swings the other way if someone gets in my way. I'll snap at my wife, or maybe some of the folks down at the senior center, if they slow me down or start questioning how I'm doing the display. So, I do feel really good and confident about it, but I just don't have much patience for anyone dragging their feet.
Even if you're going to bed at the same time, have you noticed that you're waking up much earlier than usual or feeling rested with less sleep than you normally need?

No, not really. Like I said, I go to bed when my wife does, and I usually get up around the same time I always have. I don't wake up at three in the morning or anything like that. I just get up at my normal time, but I am definitely ready to get right back to the boxes and the planning as soon as my feet hit the floor. But the hours I'm sleeping? No, they haven't changed.
Even if you're going to bed and waking up at your usual times, have you noticed that you feel rested and energized with less sleep than you normally need?

I... well, no. Like I've been saying, I'm getting my normal amount of sleep. I feel rested because I slept my regular hours, not because I'm running on less sleep. I just feel good and ready to work when I wake up. I don't feel like I could just skip sleeping or anything.

Have you had any distinct periods of time — days or more — where your mood was so elevated, irritable, or you felt so 'wired' that it was noticeably different from your usual self and observable by others?

Well, yeah, like I was saying earlier... I definitely have these stretches of time where I'm just completely wired and different. It's been going on for a while now with this memorial project. I'll feel totally lit up, you know? Just full of purpose, thinking about how the whole town is finally going to get what our family is about. 

But then, yeah, it definitely swings into being really irritable. If my wife gets in my way, or if the folks at the senior center start asking too many questions or slowing me down with the display... I just snap at them. It's definitely noticeable. My wife has certainly pointed out that I'm acting different, more on edge and intense than I usually am. So, yes, there have definitely been days at a time where I'm either on top of the world about it or just ready to bite someone's head off if they interrupt me.
